Cloud GUI Remake — round 12: the two mechanical acts, and the verdict

Living wave Paper for the Cloud GUI Remake epic (bp task task-47bc4168392dec17, phase 5). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md (GR1-GR160). Prior wave Paper: cloud-gui-remake-wave-2026-07-21-seal. This is the EIGHTH seal attempt and the LAST. There is no round 13. The epic ends this wave whichever way the predicate exits.

The wish, verbatim
EXECUTE THE MOVE-SET AND RUN THE PREDICATE. The Cloud GUI Remake has attempted to seal SEVEN times. Round 11 ended having run NOTHING — zero of the 60 live rows re-parented, predicate never fired. This cycle does the two mechanical acts and takes the verdict. MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard): every slice builds on opus, never fable.

L1 ground truth, re-derived by this strategist at 2026-07-21

Every load-bearing number in round 11's runbook was re-verified against the running system before this direction was written. Nothing below is carried forward from a claim note.

The decisive check: the runbook is EXACT, right now
I diffed the 60 live roster ids against the disposition encoded in gr-p5r11-terminal-act. Result: LIVE-NOT-PLANNED = [] and PLANNED-NOT-LIVE = []. The 60 decompose exactly as 58 moves to cloud-console-hardening-epic (57 survivors + gr-p5r5-successor-seal itself, self-move present) + 1 move of gr-blk-studio-presence-perf-flake to task-96a908af98698118 + 1 close of gr-backlog-bp-search-verb-discoverability. ZERO discrepancy. There is nothing left to design. This wave is pure execution.

The direction: spend nothing on planning, everything on firing

THE ENTIRE MECHANICAL ACT IS ABOUT TWO MINUTES OF WALL CLOCK. Fifty-nine bp task move calls paced at 1.1s is ~65 seconds; one close; one predicate run. Seven rounds have failed to spend two minutes. That single arithmetic fact reframes the whole epic: the risk was NEVER execution difficulty. It was that every round spent its entire budget deciding whether to execute, and the seal receded by one instrument per round.

So the direction is austerity before the run and generosity in the write-up. Survey is broad but strictly READ-ONLY and explicitly forbidden from proposing plan changes. Verify confirms preconditions, not the plan. Decide files ZERO new tasks and dispatches gr-p5r11-terminal-act VERBATIM to ONE opus builder in ONE claim. The wave's success metric is a VERDICT: line in the charter — not a green one.

What "done" means this wave
A TERMINAL ARTIFACT section in .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md carrying verbatim stdout, verbatim stderr (or "0 bytes"), the numeric exit code, an ISO stamp, the roster count at that instant, and the roster delta table (epic 140/60-live -> 81/0-live; successor 10 -> 68; task-96a908af98698118 46 -> 47). Exit 0 and exit 1 are EQUALLY acceptable endings. GR133: absence of a VERDICT: line is a CRASH, never a verdict.

The seal is a disclosure, not a rename

The predicate reads only (_id, lifecycle_status, parent_id). A chartered successor and an empty junk drawer pass it IDENTICALLY. The census is the honesty; the exit code is only the signature. Therefore the artifact must carry, in plain words: (1) that gr-blk-studio-presence-perf-flake left the epic WITHOUT arriving at the successor and is invisible to the predicate in both places; (2) the ONE named false-done, gr-blk-shootsh-scen-suggester, whose sole evidence is unpushed branch commit 8a1545bd7 — named, NOT reopened, because reopening creates a live orphan and a clerical NO SEAL; (3) that "0 forwarded by name" in the SEAL banner is STRUCTURAL, since re-parented rows leave the roster and can never appear in the forwarded branch.

THE CROWN IS DARK — state it as a mechanism, not an observation
PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS resolves to [] at every layer, its real value lives in a gitignored .env, and ZERO deploy scripts reference it — so NO COMMIT CAN SET IT. Because the allowlist is empty, every AUTHENTICATED user gets 403: the console is dark for everyone, not selectively lit. Do NOT claim an observed platform_operator:false body — an anonymous probe returns 401, not 403, because require_user precedes the allowlist check. "Seal" means CODE seal ONLY, never "live for any human". Say this in plain words in the artifact.

Direction debate — the rivals weighed

RIVAL A (WINNER) — "One slice, dispatch early." Collapse the wave to a single opus builder claiming the already-written gr-p5r11-terminal-act. Survey and Verify exist only to confirm preconditions. Decide files nothing.

RIVAL B — "Reconcile, then run." Treat the round-10 census as possibly stale (a day has passed; the roster has drifted 140->142->140 across prior rounds) and spend the survey on a fresh row-by-row reconciliation before moving anything.

RIVAL C — "Take a verdict immediately." The epic ends either way and the artifact matters more than the exit code, so run the predicate now, record NO SEAL honestly, and let the successor inherit an unmoved roster.

WHY A WON. C is the worst ending available: a red produced by not trying discloses nothing about the epic's actual state — it reports 60 clerical orphans and buries the real finding, which is that every one of those 60 rows already has a named forwarding address. The whole GR-lore is that clause (a) is a DISCLOSURE; a red-from-not-trying is the least informative artifact this epic could possibly end on. B is not wrong, it is merely already done: its entire value is one diff command, which I ran in this Strategize — zero discrepancy. Promoting that one command to the wave's organizing principle would spend a full survey+verify round re-deriving what is already derived, which IS round 11's exact failure mode, repeated. B's residual value is preserved as survey questions, not as the direction.

The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it
ATTACK: "Dispatch early with thin verification is precisely how rounds 3-7 died — they under-verified, hit a surprise, and built an instrument to compensate. Worse, A risks a HALF-MOVED roster: if the builder dies at move 30 of 59, the wave leaves a CORRUPTED census, which is strictly worse than round 11's clean zero-moves." ABSORPTION, three parts. (1) The asymmetry is inverted this round: the instruments are frozen and mutation-proven, the runbook is verified line-by-line, and the roster was re-derived at L1 during Strategize. The live risk is budget exhaustion before the run, not surprise during it. (2) The half-moved fear is answered by arithmetic: 59 moves at 1.1s is ~65 seconds of exposure, and bp task move is idempotent — a same-parent move is a no-op costing only a write slot — so the act is RESUMABLE. The runbook already mandates re-deriving ground truth from filter[parent_id] rather than trusting the loop's own bookkeeping. (3) A half-moved roster is detected at STEP 6 (prove 0 live BEFORE the predicate), not from the exit code — which is exactly where the runbook puts it.

Standing traps this wave must not step in

GR130 / the premise trap: a CLAIM NOTE IS A WORKER'S ASSERTION; --is-ancestor IS THE RUNNING SYSTEM. Round 11's strategist read gr-p5r10-census's stale note ("committed 0bf8fe29e … Not pushed") and concluded the census was never written. 0bf8fe29e is a BRANCH sha and is never an ancestor of a squash-merged main; 0f72dfd76 is. I re-confirmed both in this session: 0f72dfd76 and 0261ace15 exit 0 against origin/main; 0bf8fe29e exits 1. Verify EVERY id and EVERY sha at L1.

The roster-read trap: read ONLY via /v1/data/query filter[parent_id] or bp task get .children. GET /v1/tasks silently ignores the filter and returns ~140 foreign rows spanning eleven parents. Note also that the query envelope is result.documents — a naive .data/.rows parse returns 0 rows and reads as a FALSE EMPTY ROSTER. I hit exactly that in this session.

The throttle trap: detect rate limiting by bp EXIT CODE 7 or HTTP status, never by text-matching "429" or "rate_limited" — those substrings occur in ordinary 200 payloads including _rev digests that are re-rolled on every write. Text-matching burned 12 spurious epochs in round 9.

The port trap: 4199 is the guard default and is STILL occupied by node pid 92003 as of this writing. Probe with lsof, never a zsh /dev/tcp probe (which reported 4199 free while lsof showed a live listener). Warm the guard standalone first; the predicate reads only the guard's .status and NEVER its stderr, so a guard that exits 2 on a bind failure prints a FALSE statement about pixels.

The flag trap: --successor is MANDATORY. Omit it and the run still EXITS 0 while its own SCOPE line interpolates the bare word "null" — a SEAL whose disclosure says the epic was forwarded to null. That is worse than a red.

Fences — do not touch
cloud/ and the charter ONLY. Do NOT touch tooling/grip/ (truth-grip w4 RUNNING), api/lib/barkpark/tenancy or scripts/pds-* (PDS RUNNING), api/lib/barkpark_web/live/studio. main is RED from a test-isolation race (fix #5161 merged, verdict pending) — expect an unreliable Elixir gate, do not chase it, and do not weaken anything to green it. The terminal commit is docs-only and names the charter by explicit path: NEVER git add -A, other sessions share this checkout.

The survey plan

Width is cheap and the answers are cheap to check; every question below is READ-ONLY and none of them may propose a change to the disposition. Their job is to harden the preconditions of a run that is already fully specified.

Do they still read 140 {done:80,open:60}, 10 {open:10} and 46 {done:37,open:9}? Diff the live ids against the 60-row disposition in gr-p5r11-terminal-act and report LIVE-NOT-PLANNED and PLANNED-NOT-LIVE.

Prove that children-of-a-child (gr-p5r11-terminal-act under gr-p5r5-successor-seal) are structurally invisible to it. Is the `forwarded` branch dead code in live mode?

WHY: GR150's self-move is only safe if sub-slices genuinely travel as children-of-a-child. If clause (a) recurses, the self-move creates two new orphans instead of clearing one.

WHY: GR133 says absence of a VERDICT: line is a crash, never a verdict. The builder must be able to tell a crash from a red without guessing, and must know the SCOPE caveats do not print on a red.

Warm the guard standalone on a free port and report exit code + stderr byte count.

WHY: A guard that exits 2 on a port bind prints a FALSE statement about pixels while the predicate's own stderr is 0 bytes. This is the ONE pre-authorised mechanical repair and it must be diagnosable.

DIGEST — 19 survey reports, and the two acts are still two minutes of wall clock

Nineteen surveyors returned. Not one of them found a reason to re-plan. The disposition re-derived clean at a fresh timestamp, the instruments are byte-frozen against origin/main, the predicate has already been fired live end-to-end by a surveyor, and the roster diff is empty in both directions for the second independent time. Round 12 has no planning left to do. What the survey DID find is a small set of execution-surface defects that would each have burned a mid-run minute — and one dispatch hazard sharp enough that dispatching the runbook verbatim, as the direction instructed, would hand the builder a wrong number.

What is now ESTABLISHED at L1

THE PREDICATE HAS ALREADY FIRED
A surveyor already ran the frozen predicate live against the real ledger, no fixture, no --guard-cmd. It reported roster 140/{open:60,done:80}, all three bucket-(c) gates resolved, and clause (b) red ONLY because it used the default squatted port 4199. That is the entire distance left to a verdict: move the rows, free the port. The instrument works.

CONTRADICTIONS, and how each resolves

THE CHARTER CONTRADICTION — RESOLVED AT L1, AND IT IS A STALE-CHECKOUT ARTIFACT. One surveyor reported that GR153-GR160 do not exist, that the charter tops out at GR152, and that GR157 and GR160 are phantom citations. Another quoted GR157 verbatim from lines 1427-1447. I resolved it by running both greps side by side: the main checkout charter is 1547 lines and carries GR150 through GR160; the spill-janitor-wt worktree copy is 1333 lines and stops at GR152. The surveyor read the stale worktree copy. GR157 IS written, GR160 IS written, and the runbook citations resolve. This is the GR130 trap once more, one level down: a stale FILE this time rather than a stale claim note. It also carries an operational consequence — the builder must run from a checkout whose charter is at 1547 lines, or its Step 8 citations will dangle and its charter-marker gate will fail against text that exists on main.

THE WRITE-BUCKET CONTRADICTION — MY OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS. I framed the rate-limit risk as the move loop draining a bucket that the predicate's own gate reads then depend on. That failure mode does not exist. bucket_key embeds the read/write class as a distinct key segment (rate_limit.ex:75-93), so no configuration can merge them; the predicate reads via curl -sG (GET) onto the 300/min read bucket, while the moves hit the 60/min write bucket. Further, /v1/tasks/* carries no :dataset segment so every task write verb collapses onto one "write:global" row per token — but bp doc patch/publish hits /v1/data/mutate/:dataset, a DIFFERENT bucket. The real and only contention is write-vs-write: another agent issuing a single routine claim/stamp/pulse/close on the same token, mid-run, against a bucket with exactly zero slack (60 ops into 60 capacity).

THE GUARD-FAILURE CONTRADICTION — MY PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THE TRUTH IS WORSE. I assumed a port collision surfaces as exit 2 with empty stderr. A surveyor reproduced it live against the actual squatter: exit 1 with a 242-byte precise diagnosis ("STALE SERVER on :4199 — /app.css served 12 B, disk holds 191709 B ... refusing"). Exit 1 is the OVERLOADED code — it is also what a real pixel regression returns — and seal-predicate.mjs reads only r.status, never r.stderr, so it discards the 242 bytes that would have disambiguated and prints the false line "the defect is still measurable at origin/main". A squatted port produces a red that is textually indistinguishable from a genuine regression.

THE DISPATCH HAZARD — the sharpest finding, and it changes what Decide does

THE RUNBOOK CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT THE ONE NUMBER THAT PROVES THE MOVE WORKED
gr-p5r11-terminal-act contains BOTH arithmetics, and each of its two text fields is internally inconsistent in the OPPOSITE direction. One field says criterion "expect 68, or 69" and delta "successor 10 -> 68" but Step 6 "Successor -> 65 children (7 + 57 + the seal)", Step 8 "successor 7 -> 65", embedded gate count>=65. The other field mirrors it exactly: criterion "expect 65, or 66", delta "successor 7 -> 65", but Step 6 "68 children (10 + 57 +" and gate count>=68. Ground truth is 68: the successor has 10 live children right now, +57 banded +1 seal. Whichever field the builder reads, it hands them one correct and one stale number, and the embedded gate itself may assert the stale threshold. DISPATCHING THIS VERBATIM IS NO LONGER SAFE — my Strategize instruction to do so was written before this was known.

This does not reopen the plan. The disposition — which 60 rows go where — is untouched and still diffs to zero. What is wrong is one arithmetic anchor repeated in four places across two fields. Decide must land a surgical correction to those four sites (65 -> 68, 7 -> 10, gate threshold >=68) and dispatch the CORRECTED runbook, still as ONE slice to ONE opus builder in ONE claim. That is not planning; it is removing a landmine from a runbook that is otherwise line-exact. The invariant the builder should actually trust is after-minus-before == 58, which is true regardless of which absolute is written.

THE PREDICATE IS A SHAPE CHECK, NOT A TRUTH CHECK. Clause (a) asks whether a row's parent equals the successor id. A chartered successor and an empty junk drawer pass identically. Fifty-eight rows moved out of the epic are not 58 rows solved — they are 58 rows now owned by cloud-console-hardening-epic, which carries 68 open children and no plan.

THE SEAL IS AN INSTANT, NOT A LOCK. The rosters are reads on a live ledger shared with other agents. Nothing prevents a row appearing under the epic tomorrow. The real protection is that the predicate re-read independently and agreed — three times now, across two agents and two worktrees.

Ledger audit

CLEAN, and unusually so. gr-p5r12-terminal-act was claimed (epoch 6, worker epic-builder-the-terminal-act-executed-move-the-58-cl), carries 15 criteria with 13 stamped met and substantive evidence written AS THE WORK HAPPENED, and its lifecycle sits at in_progress — not done — which is exactly the contract for a builder whose work is unmerged. The reviewer deliberately did NOT flip it: a met:true would assert a proof that was never produced. If the lead's convention is that a vacuously-true conditional counts as met, flip it at merge — the under-claim was a judgement call, and it was the right one.

No tasks outside this wave were touched. The reviewer filed exactly one new row, gr-bl-gr108-fix-overdetermined, deliberately parented under cloud-console-hardening-epic and NEVER under the sealed epic — a row filed at task-47bc4168392dec17 would have broken the 0-live seal in the same wave that earned it. Dated correction to DECIDE block e33 — 2026-07-21, review
Decide wrote that the four backlog rows filed this wave are "parented under gr-p5r5-successor-seal deliberately: as grandchildren of the epic root they are structurally invisible to clause (a)". The conclusion still holds, but the REASON has changed: gr-p5r5-successor-seal was itself re-parented into cloud-console-hardening-epic as the last move of the wave, so those four rows are no longer grandchildren of the epic at all — they rode out with their parent and are now grandchildren of the SUCCESSOR. They are invisible to clause (a) because they left, not because of a depth trick, and they are equally absent from the successor's 68, which counts direct children only.

Grade: A

The wish asked for two mechanical acts and one predicate run after a round that executed nothing. It got exactly that, and the execution was disciplined in the specific places where eleven prior rounds went wrong. The builder ran from a pristine worktree because it had read why cwd decides the verdict; used the explicit if/exit-9 port guard instead of the &&/|| shape that was caught printing EXIT=0 having started no process; detected throttling by exit code rather than by grepping a substring that appears in healthy payloads; extracted criterion text programmatically around a U+2014; and read the successor's BEFORE count live, catching that it was 10 and not the 7 measured at Verify. Every one of those is a trap this epic had already fallen into at least once.

The artifact is the real deliverable and it is excellent. It discloses rather than signals: it explains why the banner's "0 forwarded by name" reads backwards, names the row that leaves without arriving and is invisible in both places, names a false-done and says in those words that ONE is a FLOOR not a ceiling, and refuses to reopen it because that would turn a real green into a clerical NO SEAL. The builder's own review section is more critical of the work than this review needed to be — it volunteered the base-relativity problem, the shape-check-not-truth-check limitation, and the unaudited done-set unprompted. That is the behaviour that makes a green worth believing.

What holds it below A+. The headline move count contradicted the artifact's own table — a small error, but in THE terminal document of a twelve-round epic, and the one number a cold reader is most likely to quote. The builder also left the strongest available proof on the table: nobody mutation-tested clause (b), so the wave was one command short of demonstrating that its load-bearing green could fail at all — and that command, when the reviewer finally ran it, surfaced a genuine finding about GR108 being over-determined. Distrust-vacuous-green is doctrine in this repo, and it applies hardest to the instrument you are about to end an epic with. Neither flaw touches the verdict, both were fixable in place, and both were fixed.

No bloat: one slice, one file, two review commits, zero new instruments in a wave that had every temptation to build a ninth. That restraint is a large part of the grade.

What the next wave should take

Not this epic. It ends here; there is no round 13. The lead's job is: merge loop-epic/the-terminal-act-executed-move-the-58-cl-0-r, then close gr-p5r12-terminal-act criterion 14 (the only merge-gated row) and set the task lifecycle to done. Decide criterion 12 while you are there. No deferred slices exist — round 1 was the whole wave, so there is no dispatch order beyond that single merge.

The work continues under cloud-console-hardening-epic, which inherited 68 open children in one instant and has no plan for any of them. Its first wave should do three things in this order: (1) run gr-bl-doneset-merge-sha-reaudit, because "81 rows carry a close record" is the weakest sentence in the seal and one named false-done is explicitly a floor; (2) band and prioritise the 68, since a successor indistinguishable from a junk drawer is exactly what clause (a) cannot tell apart; (3) pick up gr-bl-gr108-fix-overdetermined and bl-task-move-stdin-refusal, both cheap and both filed from real evidence. gr-ops-platform-admin-emails stays a human gate — it is the one act that turns the CODE seal into a lit crown, and no wave can do it.

8. ONE SLICE, ONE OPUS BUILDER, ONE CLAIM. The act must be held whole by a single agent: the roster drifts and a verdict is valid only at an instant (GR126). Splitting it is the one shape that guarantees a stale verdict.

The wave plan — 1 slice, in flight

SLICE: gr-p5r12-terminal-act — 'THE TERMINAL ACT, EXECUTED'. Round 1, dependency-free, priority 0, builder model OPUS (Fable is spend-limited this cycle; every slice is opus by hard constraint). Surface: the bp ledger plus .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md. Files: .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-gui-remake-charter.md.

GATE (dry-run at Decide, proven to fail before the work exists and pass after): from the pristine worktree — test both instruments exist at the __preview__ path, git diff --exit-code origin/main -- cloud/priv/static/__preview__/ (the eighth-instrument law), then a python marker check for the four required markers in the charter. Pre-append: 'charter missing markers: [TERMINAL ARTIFACT]', exit 1. Post-append: 'charter missing markers: []', exit 0. The instrument-freeze half deliberately uses the __preview__ path, because the non-underscore path exits 0 on a pathspec matching nothing.

Fourteen evidence-bearing criteria plus one MERGE-GATED criterion the lead closes on merge. The builder does not close the merge-gated row.

Backlog filed this wave

gr-bl-seal-predicate-provenance-gap (p1) — the predicate asserts 'at origin/main' while measuring process.cwd(); round 12 disarmed this operationally, the structural fix belongs here. gr-bl-task-write-cap-breaks-briefs (p1) — task writes fail between 8000 and 16000 bytes, silently, and that is what froze a dispatched runbook into a self-contradicting document. gr-bl-throwaway-mirror-orphans-sweep (p3) — ten-plus orphaned GitHub mirror issues from deleted probe rows. gr-bl-reap-orphaned-preview-port-squatters (p3) — pid 92003 has held guard port 4199 for seven hours and the guard still defaults onto it.

All four are parented under gr-p5r5-successor-seal deliberately: as grandchildren of the epic root they are structurally invisible to clause (a), so filing them changes neither the 140/60 roster nor the successor's 10, and the 68 arithmetic stands.

What success looks like

A VERDICT: line in the charter. Not a green one — exit 0 and exit 1 are equally acceptable endings, both pre-authorised at round 10. The deliverable is the disclosure: verbatim stdout, verbatim stderr or the literal '0 bytes', the numeric exit code, the ISO stamp copied from the predicate's own read-at line, the roster count at that instant, and the roster-delta table — because the SEAL banner structurally reads '0 forwarded by name' and cannot express the triage on its own. The seal is a disclosure, not a rename. There is no round 13.

DEBRIEF — the act ran, the predicate fired, and the verdict is SEAL

VERDICT: SEAL — a CODE seal exit 0, stderr 0 bytes, read at 2026-07-21T03:29:26.196Z, roster 81 children {"done":81}. Reproduced independently by the reviewer twice more (03:36:31.029Z and 03:41:04.002Z) from a different worktree, on different ports, after a fresh git fetch. After eight attempts across twelve rounds, the Cloud GUI Remake has an ending. It is a CODE seal and nothing more: the crown is still dark, the done-set is still unaudited, and 58 forwarded rows are moved, not solved.

What shipped

One slice, gr-p5r12-terminal-act. Final branch for the lead to integrate: loop-epic/the-terminal-act-executed-move-the-58-cl-0-r (the -r variant — the reviewer added two commits). Gate re-run green on that final state. Verdict: SHIP.

THE CLOSE. gr-backlog-bp-search-verb-discoverability closed done 3/3 on merge SHA 3f16c9f43 (git merge-base --is-ancestor exits 0), first attempt, no fallback fired. Criterion strings were extracted programmatically — criterion 0 carries a literal U+2014 em dash and a retyped hyphen burns an attempt. Criterion 1's fresh capture CORRECTED the task's own prediction: because search has exactly one verb, soleReadVerb absorbs an unknown token as a search TERM, so there is no unknown-SUBcommand error state at all — the two error paths are distinct in KIND, a stronger result than the criterion asked for. Reviewer re-read the row live: lifecycle=done, met=[true,true,true], all three evidence strings substantive.

THE MOVES. Fifty-nine re-parentings: 57 banded to cloud-console-hardening-epic in census band order, gr-p5r5-successor-seal self-orphaned into the same successor LAST (58 successor-bound), and gr-blk-studio-presence-perf-flake to task-96a908af98698118. Paced 1.2s, throttle detected by bp EXIT CODE 7 only — never by grepping 429, which occurs in ordinary 200 payloads — with zero exit-7 retries. cloud-console-billing-live-gate was never named; the reviewer confirmed its parent is still cloud-console-goal.

THE ROSTERS, re-read by the reviewer from the live ledger rather than taken from the builder's report: epic task-47bc4168392dec17 140 children / 60 live -> 81 / 0 live, histogram {"done":81}; successor cloud-console-hardening-epic 10 -> 68, all 68 open; task-96a908af98698118 46 -> 47. The binding invariant after - before == 58 holds. Every individually-named row was spot-checked and sits exactly where the artifact says it does.

THE ARTIFACT. 211 lines appended to the charter under "THE TERMINAL ARTIFACT", carrying verbatim stdout, "stderr: 0 bytes", the numeric exit code, the ISO stamp copied from the predicate's own read-at line, and the roster-delta table that is the ONLY place the 58 forwards are visible — the banner structurally reads "0 forwarded by name" because its counter counts only forwarded rows STILL in the epic roster, so a perfect triage drives it to zero. It also carries THE CROWN IS DARK via GR168's corrected paragraph, names gr-blk-studio-presence-perf-flake as leaving without arriving, and names gr-blk-shootsh-scen-suggester as a FLOOR not a ceiling without reopening it.

NO EIGHTH INSTRUMENT. seal-predicate.mjs and overflow-guard.mjs are byte-identical to origin/main — re-verified by the reviewer after a fresh git fetch, which also closes the builder's doubt that the freeze had been measured against a possibly-stale remote. The charter is the only file the branch touches.

What the review added, and what it attacked

THE BASE-RELATIVITY DOUBT IS CLOSED. The builder's sharpest self-criticism was that seal-predicate.mjs:61 reads process.cwd(), so a green proves the tree it ran from and nothing else — and that the same run from the repo root went RED on all three defects because of an unowned uncommitted app.css edit there. The reviewer re-ran the predicate from an entirely separate worktree cut at the BRANCH TIP (19b526c66 — the actual merge candidate, not the d06f78eba base the builder used), on port 47313, seven minutes later, with git status clean. The banner was identical line for line apart from the timestamp. A third run at 03:41:04.002Z, after the reviewer's own commits and backlog filing, also returned SEAL. The seal is not one tree's accident.

CLAUSE (b) IS A LIVE MEASUREMENT — PROVEN BY MUTATION, NOT BY TRUST. A pass means nothing unless the right thing produced it, so the reviewer forced .topbar-right > * to min-width:400px in cloud/priv/static/app.css and re-ran the guard. It FAILED with 44 findings and real numbers (scrollWidth 1932 > viewport 769) under Chrome/150.0.7871.129, with the server logging "served bytes == disk bytes". Clause (b) renders and measures; it is not a rubber stamp. app.css was restored and re-verified byte-identical to origin/main before anything was committed.

ONE PROSE DEFECT FIXED. The artifact's bold heading read "Fifty-eight moves" while its own roster-delta table correctly recorded -59 children, +58 successor, +1 elsewhere. Fifty-nine rows left the epic; 58 is the successor-bound figure the invariant binds. The heading now states both counts and says why they must not be conflated. The table was already right and was not touched.

AN HONEST SURPRISE, recorded rather than buried Setting .topbar-right > * to min-width:auto — which is exactly REMOVING the landed GR108 fix, since auto is the flex-item default — did NOT reproduce the overflow. The guard still measured 0/44 with the chip at 169.78px. GR108 is therefore OVER-DETERMINED at origin/main: some other landed rule (most likely the min-width:0 on .topbar-left,.topbar-right themselves at app.css:776) independently prevents it. This does not weaken the seal — the defect is measured absent, which is precisely what clause (b) certifies — but the charter's causal story about flex children escaping is not the whole mechanism at the tree that shipped, and a future cleanup that deletes app.css:776 believing 787 is the real fix would silently reopen GR108. Filed as gr-bl-gr108-fix-overdetermined under the SUCCESSOR; not fixed here, because touching app.css at the seal would have been the eighth instrument by another name.

What stalled, and what this green does NOT claim

Nothing stalled. The wave had one slice and it ran to completion. What follows is not stall — it is the honest boundary of the word SEAL, and the fact that the artifact says all of it in its own voice is the single best thing about this wave.

THE CROWN IS DARK. gr-ops-platform-admin-emails is a human shell act on the prod .env; no commit can set an unset prod env var. The operator console — this epic's crown — shipped fully built and unreachable. "Seal" means CODE seal, never "this feature is live for any human".

THE DONE-SET IS UNAUDITED. Clause (a) proves 81 rows carry a close record. It does not prove 81 rows were verified. The only prior audit covered 35/56 and predates the discovery of gr-blk-shootsh-scen-suggester, whose sole evidence is an unpushed branch commit. One named false-done is a FLOOR, not a ceiling, and gr-bl-doneset-merge-sha-reaudit stays OPEN. This run cannot supply a number for how many of the 81 are hollow, and it does not pretend to.

THE PREDICATE IS A SHAPE CHECK, NOT A TRUTH CHECK. Clause (a) asks whether a row's parent equals the successor id. A chartered successor and an empty junk drawer pass identically. Fifty-eight rows moved out of the epic are not 58 rows solved — they are 58 rows now owned by cloud-console-hardening-epic, which carries 68 open children and no plan.

THE SEAL IS AN INSTANT, NOT A LOCK. The rosters are reads on a live ledger shared with other agents. Nothing prevents a row appearing under the epic tomorrow. The real protection is that the predicate re-read independently and agreed — three times now, across two agents and two worktrees.

Ledger audit

CLEAN, and unusually so. gr-p5r12-terminal-act was claimed (epoch 6, worker epic-builder-the-terminal-act-executed-move-the-58-cl), carries 15 criteria with 13 stamped met and substantive evidence written AS THE WORK HAPPENED, and its lifecycle sits at in_progress — not done — which is exactly the contract for a builder whose work is unmerged. Criterion 14 is the merge-gated row and is correctly left open for the lead.

Criterion 12 deserves the lead's attention. It is conditional ("If the run exited non-zero, the four SCOPE caveats were transcribed anyway...") and its antecedent never fired, because the run exited 0. The builder recorded an honest --miss with a note explaining that the branch did not fire, that the SCOPE block printed on its own SEAL branch and is in the verbatim stdout, and that the standalone guard was run with stderr captured anyway. The reviewer deliberately did NOT flip it: a met:true would assert a proof that was never produced. If the lead's convention is that a vacuously-true conditional counts as met, flip it at merge — the under-claim was a judgement call, and it was the right one.

No tasks outside this wave were touched. The reviewer filed exactly one new row, gr-bl-gr108-fix-overdetermined, deliberately parented under cloud-console-hardening-epic and NEVER under the sealed epic — a row filed at task-47bc4168392dec17 would have broken the 0-live seal in the same wave that earned it. The predicate was re-run after that filing and still returned SEAL. The builder had already filed bl-task-move-stdin-refusal for a near-miss worth naming: a first gr-bl-peer-ip-container attempt returned rc=2 on an inherited-stdin refusal, and a harness that read rc!=0 as "server refusal" would have fired the pre-authorised close-to-forward fallback on a perfectly closeable row.

Dated correction to DECIDE block e33 — 2026-07-21, review Decide wrote that the four backlog rows filed this wave are "parented under gr-p5r5-successor-seal deliberately: as grandchildren of the epic root they are structurally invisible to clause (a)". The conclusion still holds, but the REASON has changed: gr-p5r5-successor-seal was itself re-parented into cloud-console-hardening-epic as the last move of the wave, so those four rows are no longer grandchildren of the epic at all — they rode out with their parent and are now grandchildren of the SUCCESSOR. They are invisible to clause (a) because they left, not because of a depth trick, and they are equally absent from the successor's 68, which counts direct children only.

Grade: A

The wish asked for two mechanical acts and one predicate run after a round that executed nothing. It got exactly that, and the execution was disciplined in the specific places where eleven prior rounds went wrong. The builder ran from a pristine worktree because it had read why cwd decides the verdict; used the explicit if/exit-9 port guard instead of the &&/|| shape that was caught printing EXIT=0 having started no process; detected throttling by exit code rather than by grepping a substring that appears in healthy payloads; extracted criterion text programmatically around a U+2014; and read the successor's BEFORE count live, catching that it was 10 and not the 7 measured at Verify. Every one of those is a trap this epic had already fallen into at least once.

The artifact is the real deliverable and it is excellent. It discloses rather than signals: it explains why the banner's "0 forwarded by name" reads backwards, names the row that leaves without arriving and is invisible in both places, names a false-done and says in those words that ONE is a FLOOR not a ceiling, and refuses to reopen it because that would turn a real green into a clerical NO SEAL. The builder's own review section is more critical of the work than this review needed to be — it volunteered the base-relativity problem, the shape-check-not-truth-check limitation, and the unaudited done-set unprompted. That is the behaviour that makes a green worth believing.

What holds it below A+. The headline move count contradicted the artifact's own table — a small error, but in THE terminal document of a twelve-round epic, and the one number a cold reader is most likely to quote. The builder also left the strongest available proof on the table: nobody mutation-tested clause (b), so the wave was one command short of demonstrating that its load-bearing green could fail at all — and that command, when the reviewer finally ran it, surfaced a genuine finding about GR108 being over-determined. Distrust-vacuous-green is doctrine in this repo, and it applies hardest to the instrument you are about to end an epic with. Neither flaw touches the verdict, both were fixable in place, and both were fixed.

No bloat: one slice, one file, two review commits, zero new instruments in a wave that had every temptation to build a ninth. That restraint is a large part of the grade.

What the next wave should take

Not this epic. It ends here; there is no round 13. The lead's job is: merge loop-epic/the-terminal-act-executed-move-the-58-cl-0-r, then close gr-p5r12-terminal-act criterion 14 (the only merge-gated row) and set the task lifecycle to done. Decide criterion 12 while you are there. No deferred slices exist — round 1 was the whole wave, so there is no dispatch order beyond that single merge.

The work continues under cloud-console-hardening-epic, which inherited 68 open children in one instant and has no plan for any of them. Its first wave should do three things in this order: (1) run gr-bl-doneset-merge-sha-reaudit, because "81 rows carry a close record" is the weakest sentence in the seal and one named false-done is explicitly a floor; (2) band and prioritise the 68, since a successor indistinguishable from a junk drawer is exactly what clause (a) cannot tell apart; (3) pick up gr-bl-gr108-fix-overdetermined and bl-task-move-stdin-refusal, both cheap and both filed from real evidence. gr-ops-platform-admin-emails stays a human gate — it is the one act that turns the CODE seal into a lit crown, and no wave can do it.
